caption: A rubber ball is dropped from shoulder height onto a concrete driveway and bounces several times before rolling away.

sa.check: A rubber ball is dropped from about shoulder height.
It lands on a concrete driveway.
The ball is dropped rather than thrown.
The drop comes first, then the bounces, then the roll.

pc.expect: Each bounce is lower than the one before, none higher than the drop, and the bounces get quicker as they shrink.
pc.fail: A bounce is higher than the one before it; or the bounces stay the same height; or the ball stops dead on first contact with no bounce.

pc.expect: The ball comes down straight from the hand and bounces close to vertical, drifting only a little before rolling.
pc.fail: The ball shoots off sideways at the first bounce on the flat concrete; or it reverses direction between bounces; or it jinks in mid-air.

pc.expect: It falls quicker as it drops, and after each bounce it comes down again.
pc.fail: The ball hangs at the top of a bounce; or it rises after the last bounce; or it floats.

pc.expect: The ball squashes briefly at each contact and springs back round, and the concrete stays unmarked.
pc.fail: The ball stays flat after a bounce; or it sinks into the concrete; or it splashes.
The ball vanishes or a second one appears; or it turns into another object; or it passes through the driveway.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The ball's colour and the driveway stay the same.
pc.fail: The ball changes colour or size; or the driveway's cracks shift between frames; or the surroundings rearrange.
